_about: Declarative data for Engine Sound Lab: engine layouts with their firing angles, intake/exhaust hardware, gearing and presets. The DSP code reads numbers from here and holds none of its own. Firing entries are [cylinder, crank angle in degrees within one cycle, bank]. A four-stroke cycle is 720 degrees of crank; a rotary's is 360 degrees of eccentric shaft.

R4.label: Four-rotor Wankel
R4._note: Even 90-degree spacing of the eccentric shaft; the R26B's rotor order is not published.

Radial9.label: Nine-cylinder radial
Radial9._note: Odd-numbered radials fire every other cylinder around the case: 1-3-5-7-9-2-4-6-8, every 80 degrees.

V8-2T.label: V8 two-stroke (uniflow diesel)
V8-2T._note: A two-stroke fires every cylinder once per revolution: eight cylinders fire every 45 degrees. Uniflow scavenging: ports in, poppet exhaust valves out.

blockNoise._source: Combustion noise radiated by the block and heads, one short noise burst per firing scaled by load^loadExp (so the idle, fitted to the real S65, is untouched). Calibrated against Gran Turismo 7's engine-bay microphones (calibrate.py --vs bay --layer Eng), where airbox and cone-filter engines had come out up to 2.5 octaves too dark.

loadUnevenness._source: Gran Turismo 7's engine recordings, 19 engines matched to presets: from behind, the orders below the firing order rise from about -22 dB at idle to about -10 dB above 70% of the rev limit at full load, where the synth had them flat near -30. Each cylinder gets a fixed pulse-strength (amp) and arrival (timing, a fraction of the firing interval) difference, scaled by load x (base + (1 - base) x speed^curve); at idle load it all but vanishes, keeping the idle as clean as the real S65 (half orders 30-52 dB down). The pattern has its once- and twice-per-cycle components removed (removeLowOrders), which kept the 63 Hz octave from behind from rising up to 9 dB above GT7's. Intake pulses get intakeScale times the difference: GT7's intake microphones hear stronger half orders than its exhaust ones, while its engine-bay microphones hear weaker ones; 2 keeps both within 6 dB.

cycleVariance._source: Real S65 warm idle: cycle-energy CV 0.14 with half-orders 30-50 dB below firing, so most variation drifts over several cycles rather than jumping per firing (STE-035).

coldStart._source: STE-035 (BMW S65 cold start, rear exhaust): idle eases from 1,214 rpm to the warm 786 over ~60 s; the exhaust stays ~9 dB louder at the same rpm until ~79 s, then falls within ~6 s as catalyst heating ends; cycle CV 0.21 cold against 0.14 warm.

drivetrain._driveFriction: The engine friction term is tuned for how fast a free-revving engine slows down, and takes 30-45% of torque at speed; a real engine loses 10-20%. Driving a car, friction is scaled by this factor (free revving is unchanged).
drivetrain._gearbox: Gear-pair mesh counts are derived, not listed: a pair on a fixed centre distance has a constant tooth sum, so per input-shaft revolution the pair for ratio g meshes pairTeethSum / (headRatio + g) times (two-shaft bike boxes: headRatio 1 and no head set). In a layshaft car box a ratio of exactly 1.000 is direct drive, with no loaded gear pair at all.

layshaft._note: In-line manual box: head set, layshaft, direct-drive top-but-one gear.

transaxle._note: Two-shaft box (transaxles, dual-clutch, race sequentials): every gear is a loaded pair.

bike._note: Motorcycle cassette box with chain or belt final drive (no hypoid pinion).

direct._note: No gearbox: one ratio through the rear axle only (a Top Fuel dragster).

car.label: Car (E9x M3 six-speed)
car._source: BMW E9x M3 Getrag six-speed ratios, 3.846 final drive, 1,650 kg, 18-inch wheels.

race-car.label: Single-seater race car (eight-speed)
race-car._source: Typical open-wheel figures: 750 kg with driver, high drag from downforce, about 100 km/h in 1st and 340 km/h in 8th at 18,000 rpm.

sportbike.label: Sport bike (six-speed, chain)
sportbike._source: Typical litre sport bike: 260 kg with rider, primary and chain reduction folded into one final ratio.

cruiser.label: Cruiser motorcycle (six-speed, belt)
cruiser._source: Typical big V-twin cruiser: 420 kg with rider.

dirtbike.label: Dirt bike (five-speed, chain)
dirtbike._source: Typical 450 cc motocross bike: 190 kg with rider, knobbly tyres.

real-audi-quattro-s1-e2.label: Audi Sport quattro S1 E2 (Group B, 1985)

real-audi-r10-tdi.label: Audi R10 TDI (2006 Le Mans winner)

drivetrain._grip: Tyre grip mu: road tyres about 1.0; race slicks about 1.7 before downforce; a motorcycle about 1.0 (the wheelie and traction limit is near 1 g); a Top Fuel dragster's tyres and track prep about 4.
drivetrain._traction: Grip comes from the driven axle: its static share of the weight plus load transfer (CG height over wheelbase times acceleration in g); all-wheel drive uses all of it; a rear-driven bike is also limited by the front wheel lifting.

autoShift._about: Automatic shifting, racing style: up at the limiter under throttle; down as soon as the lower gear would not over-rev, whenever the driver is off the throttle or braking. (Under throttle a downshift would undo the upshift just made and oscillate.)

rear.label: Behind the car
rear.note: Fitted to a recording made behind a BMW S65's tailpipes.
rear._source: Octave EQ fitted by scripts/fit-perspectives.py to STE-035 (Zoom H4n behind the BMW S65's tailpipes), warm idle 95-112 s.

front.label: In front, at the intake
front.note: Fitted to a recording made at a BMW S65's front intake.
front._source: Octave EQ fitted to STE-036 (H4n at the front intake of the S65), warm idle 52-75 s. Level is matched to the rear at full throttle; in the recordings this position was 16 dB quieter than the rear at warm idle (same recorder, gain assumed unchanged).

bay.label: Engine bay, hood open
bay.note: Fitted to a recording made in a BMW S65's open engine bay.
bay._source: Octave EQ fitted to STE-037 (H4n in the S65's open engine bay), warm idle 35-78 s; below 30 Hz the take is handling noise and is not fitted. Level is matched to the rear at full throttle; in the recordings this position was 11 dB quieter than the rear at warm idle (same recorder, gain assumed unchanged).

cabin.label: Driver's seat
cabin.note: Estimated: there is no recording from inside the car yet.
cabin._source: No recording: estimated. The body blocks the mid and high frequencies, the cabin booms around 60-80 Hz, and the room is small.

dry.label: Dry model (no listener)
dry.note: The synthesizer's raw output: every source at full level, no body, distance, ground or room.
dry._source: The synthesizer's raw output with every source at full level: no body, distance, ground or room.

straight.label: Straight pipe
straight._source: Was lpHz 8500 / rasp 0.7: every straight-piped preset measured against Gran Turismo's recordings came out too bright from behind (787B +2.8 octaves against GT7, NASCAR +1.8 and Formula 1 +1.0 against GT5/GT6, quattro S1 +0.4). 3000 / 0.5 puts the 787B and quattro within 0.7 octave of GT7, the spread between two microphones on one recording.

twinscrew.label: Twin-screw
twinscrew._source: Whine levels were cut 8.5 dB (2026-11-15) when the whine got its own per-position weight (perspectives sources.blower): against Gran Turismo 7's Hellcat, the twin-screw's whine is about 2.5 dB under all energy at the blower inlet but 19.5 dB under it in the engine bay and 29 dB under it in the cabin.

rev-sweep.label: Slow sweep to the limiter and back

pull-and-brake.label: Pull through the gears, then brake to a stop
